name: NanoClaw
vibe_summary: A radically minimal OpenClaw alternative where each agent runs in its own Linux container with real OS-level isolation instead of app-level permission checks. Small enough to read end-to-end, with per-agent Slack apps, memory, and scheduled jobs on Anthropic's Agents SDK.

Running multiple isolated agents with separate identities
Self-hosters comfortable with Docker and Node tooling

You want a managed, zero-setup hosted experience

Codebase small enough to fully audit and understand
Fewer dependencies and config files reduce attack surface
Per-agent Slack apps with automatic provisioning

Younger project with less battle-testing at scale
Requires Docker and more hands-on setup

overview_markdown:
NanoClaw is a deliberately minimal reimplementation of OpenClaw's core idea: a personal AI assistant reachable over WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Gmail, and iMessage, with persistent memory and scheduled jobs. The author's stated motivation is trust — OpenClaw's ~500k lines, 53 config files, and 70+ dependencies were too much to audit, so NanoClaw compresses the same core functionality into one process and a handful of files running on Anthropic's Agents SDK.

The defining architectural difference is isolation. Where OpenClaw enforces security at the application layer (allowlists, pairing codes) inside a single shared Node process, NanoClaw runs each agent in its own Linux container with filesystem isolation. A credential gateway brokers Anthropic credentials so agents never hold raw keys, and recent commits show active hardening: CA trust fixes for TLS-inspecting gateways, log redaction that survives BigInt/cycle edge cases, and a pinned Baileys release to patch a WhatsApp message-spoofing CVE.

Operationally it targets self-hosters: a `nanoclaw.sh` bootstrap installs Node, pnpm, and Docker, builds the agent container, and pairs channels, with Claude Code auto-invoked to diagnose failed steps. Recent work added update channels (stable/beta/edge) and per-agent Slack app provisioning, signaling a maturing project — though the ecosystem and feature surface remain far smaller than OpenClaw's.
